scope: Durable restore operation IDs and bounded parent-interruption recovery
boundaries: VALIDATED after child/output checks but before pointer replacement
POINTER_COMMITTED after pointer replacement before final operation acknowledgement
LIVE_OWNER refusal then controlled termination of owned helper
CHILD_IN_FLIGHT marker conservatively blocked; no real in-flight Pulse termination qualified
normal_cases: Native first request and repeated ID after reopening, no new attempt
Changed parameters under same ID rejected
Older committed ID replay does not rewind a later pointer
recovery_rules: PID plus process creation time, not PID alone
Persist intent and lifecycle stages with fsync plus atomic same-directory receipt replace
Recover only when original owner is proven dead or PID reused
Committed pointer already present can recover lost reply; validated uncommitted output never adopted
Move attributable dead-owner locks to quarantine, preserve bytes
Interrupted ID never silently reruns; explicit new ID required
limits: Windows process exits, not power failure or disk-full guarantees
No external events or physiological model changes
No new restorable checkpoint or broader rollback qualification
